title: The Zulu club then and now
summary: Williams dislikes the Zulus' ragged dress, thinks they dressed better last year, and recalls playing on their truck for white people.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What about the Azulis? How old were they?
Oh, they're old. I can't tell you how old they is.
They were here when you got here?

Yeah, they're going out. A fella told me the other night the Azulis was going out. I don't like to see the Azulis. The Azulis look like you're just trying to make it. I don't like them at all. And I used to be playing on the truck. I used to play it with white people, with white people. They had to see the Azulis. I said, well, this is my part. You don't need to go to see the Azulis. But last year they was a little bit better.
I was there last year. I got a coconut. Gave it to a girl from England. Yeah. Came all the way across the waters.
You think they were better last year. What do you mean? What?
I mean they dressed a little bit better. Yeah.
Did they dress ratty in the old days? Worse they do now?
Oh, yes. Like they're just trying to make it. They just put it on like that, you know?
Mm-hmm. Well, they must have plenty of money though.
They got more money now than everyone's had. Got more money now than everyone's had.
I guess you must know some people in the Azulis.
I know them. Know plenty about it. See them but don't know the name.
